parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: You have a vertical spring of unknown spring constant, cylinders of unknown masses, a digital scale and a stopwatch. Design an experiment to determine the spring constant. State what to measure, how to reduce uncertainty, and what graph to use.

answer.text: Measure each attached mass m with the scale. Displace it slightly and time several complete oscillations, repeating each measurement. Calculate T = total time/number of oscillations. Repeat for several masses. Plot T² against m; its gradient s = 4π²/k, so k = 4π²/s. Keep oscillations small and do not exceed the spring’s elastic range.

evidence.question: 2a-b
evidence.review: Worked answer checked against the source marking guidance; wording adapted for independent IB practice.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
A block of mass M oscillates on a horizontal ideal spring with amplitude d₀ and negligible friction. In a second trial an identical block is attached to it, and the same spring oscillates with the same amplitude. Compare the maximum speed and maximum kinetic energy.

A. Maximum speed is greater in trial 1; maximum kinetic energy is greater in trial 1.
B. Maximum speed is greater in trial 1; maximum kinetic energy is the same.
C. Both are the same in the two trials.
D. Maximum speed is the same; maximum kinetic energy is greater in trial 2.

answer.text: B. The same spring deformation stores the same energy, so both trials reach the same maximum kinetic energy. Sharing that energy between a larger mass gives a smaller maximum speed.

evidence.review: Checked source answer/scoring guide and independently worked adapted version.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
A simple pendulum and a mass on an ideal spring each have a period of 1.0 s on Earth. They are moved to a planet where gravitational field strength is twice Earth’s. Both undergo small oscillations. How do their periods compare with their Earth values?

A. Both periods decrease.
B. Both periods remain the same.
C. The spring period decreases; the pendulum period is unchanged.
D. The pendulum period decreases; the spring period is unchanged.

answer.text: D. For the pendulum, T = 2π√(l/g), so its period decreases by a factor √2. For the spring, T = 2π√(m/k), which is independent of g.

evidence.review: Checked source answer/scoring guide and independently worked adapted version.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: An ideal horizontal mass–spring system oscillates without friction between x = −x₀ and x = +x₀. Sketch energy bars for kinetic energy and spring potential energy at x = −x₀, x = 0 and x = +x₀. Use the same scale and take spring potential energy as zero at equilibrium.

answer.text: At both turning points, kinetic energy is zero and spring potential energy equals the total energy. At equilibrium, spring potential energy is zero and kinetic energy equals the same total energy. The total height of the two bars is unchanged at all three positions.

evidence.review: Checked source answer/scoring guide and independently worked adapted version.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: The displacement graph shows a mass oscillating on an ideal spring. Its spring constant is given as k = F_max/x₀. Derive the mass in terms of F_max, x₀ and t₀.

answer.text: The time between successive identical turning points is T = 2t₀. Using T = 2π√(m/k), m = kT²/(4π²) = F_max t₀²/(π²x₀).

evidence.review: Checked source answer/scoring guide and independently worked adapted version.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
The graph shows acceleration a against displacement x for a pendulum undergoing small oscillations.

(a) Explain why the graph indicates simple harmonic motion.
(b) Determine the oscillation period.

answer.text:
(a) The straight line through the origin shows a ∝ x, and its negative gradient shows acceleration is directed opposite to displacement. Thus a = −ω²x.
(b) Using approximately a = −13 cm s⁻² at x = +1.2 cm, ω² = 13/1.2 = 10.8 s⁻². Therefore T = 2π/√10.8 = 1.91 s ≈ 1.9 s.

evidence.review: Source question, official answer and adapted solution checked individually.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
A pendulum-period expression has the form T = 2π(L/g)ⁿ, where L is length and g is acceleration. For the equation to have consistent dimensions, what must n be?

A. −2
B. −½
C. ½
D. 2

answer.text: C. L/g has units m/(m s⁻²) = s². Therefore (s²)ⁿ must equal s, giving 2n = 1 and n = ½.

evidence.review: Source question, official answer and adapted solution checked individually.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: State the defining condition for simple harmonic motion.

answer.text: Acceleration is directly proportional to displacement from a fixed equilibrium point and is always directed towards that point: a = −ω²x, with constant ω.

evidence.review: Source question, official answer and adapted solution checked individually.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
A crystal surface performs simple harmonic motion. Its displacement–time graph is shown.

(a) Determine its period and angular frequency.
(b) Determine its maximum acceleration.

answer.text:
(a) Four cycles take 0.60 μs, so T = 0.15 μs = 1.5 × 10⁻⁷ s and ω = 2π/T = 4.19 × 10⁷ rad s⁻¹.
(b) Amplitude is 40 μm = 4.0 × 10⁻⁵ m. Thus a_max = ω²x₀ ≈ 7.0 × 10¹⁰ m s⁻², or 7.1 × 10¹⁰ m s⁻² using the rounded ω = 4.2 × 10⁷.

evidence.review: Source question, official answer and adapted solution checked individually.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A floating pencil displaced vertically by y experiences resultant force F = -Aρgy, where A, ρ and g are constant. (1) Show that it moves with simple harmonic motion. (2) Its period is T = 2π√(l/g), with l = 85 mm. It is displaced 5.0 mm and released. Calculate the maximum acceleration.

answer.text:
Editorial worked explanation, checked against the official mark scheme:

A vertical displacement y changes buoyant force by Aρgy, so ma = -Aρgy and acceleration is proportional and opposite to displacement: SHM. With the supplied period formula, ω = sqrt(g/l), so a_max = ω²y_max = (9.81/0.085)(0.0050) = 0.58 m s^-2.
answer.evidence: Official mark scheme checked on page 23.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
A mass attached to two springs oscillates horizontally in simple harmonic motion between turning points P and Q, as shown. Which quantity has minimum magnitude when the mass is at Q?

A. Acceleration of the mass
B. Kinetic energy of the mass
C. Potential energy of the mass–spring system
D. Resultant force of the springs on the mass

answer.text:
Published key B checked; editorial worked explanation:

B. Q is a turning point, so the mass is instantaneously at rest and its kinetic energy is zero, the minimum possible value. Its displacement magnitude is maximum there, so the spring potential energy, restoring-force magnitude and acceleration magnitude are all maximum.

evidence.detail: AQA 7408/1 June 2023 published key B, mark-scheme PDF page 28; explanation independently authored and checked.

cross-aq24p1-32:whole.hint: Write a period expression for each oscillator, then compare what changes on moving planets.
notes: A simple pendulum has T = 2π√(L/g), while an ideal mass–spring oscillator has T = 2π√(m/k). Gravity changes the pendulum period but only shifts the spring’s equilibrium position.

cross-ap24p1-written-2a-b:whole.hint: The available equipment can measure an oscillation period even though it cannot directly measure extension.
notes: Linearise T = 2π√(m/k) by squaring it. Timing many cycles reduces the fractional effect of reaction time; identify the gradient before rearranging for k.

cross-ap1ced-mcq-7:whole.hint: Compare the stored energy at the turning points before comparing speeds at equilibrium.
notes: This is a qualitative energy comparison. Equal maximum kinetic energy does not imply equal maximum speed when the moving masses differ.

cross-ap1ced-mcq-12:whole.hint: Write the two period relationships and identify which contains g.
notes: Gravity changes a vertical spring’s equilibrium extension, but not its small-oscillation period when m and k stay fixed.

cross-ap1ced-written-2-A:whole.hint: Identify where the oscillator stops and where it moves fastest.
notes: Spring potential energy is non-negative on both sides of equilibrium. A negative displacement does not mean negative elastic energy; the spring is deformed in either direction.

cross-ap1ced-written-2-Bii:whole.hint: Measure a full cycle on the graph before rearranging the period equation.
notes: Going from one extreme to the opposite extreme takes half a period. Using T = t₀ instead of 2t₀ would make the inferred mass four times too small.

cross-ca25n42-written-5-ai-aii:whole.hint: The slope is linked to angular frequency squared. Check the sign as well as whether the line is straight.
notes: The minus sign describes the restoring direction. The square root of the slope magnitude gives ω, not the ordinary frequency f.
The centimetre units cancel in a/x because both axes use cm. Converting just one axis to metres would introduce a factor-of-100 error.

cross-ca25j12-mcq-4:whole.hint: Find the units of L/g before considering its power.
notes: The factor 2π is dimensionless. Dimensional consistency can establish the exponent here, but cannot determine a numerical prefactor by itself.

cross-ca25j42-written-5-a:whole.hint: A restoring acceleration needs both a direction condition and a proportionality condition.
notes: An acceleration towards equilibrium alone does not establish SHM: its magnitude must be proportional to displacement. The minus sign expresses the opposite directions of a and x.

cross-ca25m42-written-4-a-b:whole.hint: Read a complete cycle and the maximum displacement from equilibrium, taking care with the micro-unit scales.
notes: Amplitude is half the peak-to-peak displacement. Maximum acceleration occurs at maximum displacement, although the velocity is zero there.

cross-fast-aqa-f44747ff7b639a5d-6-c1:who.hint: Show both proportionality to displacement and the restoring direction.
notes: To establish SHM, show acceleration is proportional to displacement and directed toward equilibrium; the negative sign expresses the restoring direction.
The supplied period gives ω² = g/l. Maximum acceleration is ω² times the amplitude; use metres for both l and the 5.0 mm displacement.

cross-fast-production-006-a-q31:whole.hint: Identify which motion quantities are zero and which are largest at an extreme displacement in simple harmonic motion.
notes: A turning point has zero instantaneous speed even though the restoring force and acceleration are greatest in magnitude.
The result uses qualitative SHM energy changes, which the current IB guide places at standard level.
